outline.chapter_title: From LSTMs to Transformers: The Design Crisis of Sequential Models
outline.description: This chapter introduces the historical context of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), focusing on the profound success and eventual dominance of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks before the emergence of Transformers. It establishes the baseline capabilities of LSTMs in handling sequential data and sets up the critical problem statement: How can we recover the size-scaling benefits of RNNs while overcoming their architectural bottlenecks?
subtopics: The Triumph of LSTMs: Solving the Vanishing Gradient Problem
The Architecture of LSTM: Gating Mechanisms and the Constant Error Carousel
The Rise of Transformers: Parallelism, Attention, and Scale
The Inflexibility of Memory Mixing (Exemplified by Nearest Neighbor Search)
Bottlenecks in Storage Capacity (Scalar vs. Vector Limitations)
Sequential Loss: The Lack of Hardware-Parallelizability
